name: Kangaroo Island Wilderness Trail
reason: Named by the tourism board as a well-known multi-day trail through Flinders Chase (a Great-Walk style long trail, campsites on route); a long trail is a spot.

name: Cape du Couedic Lighthouse
reason: Wikivoyage lists it under Lighthouses and the board names it with Admirals Arch; remains of storerooms and flying fox a short walk away. Exterior only, but a guide-singled-out landmark.

name: Weirs Cove
reason: Wikivoyage lists only 'Weirs Lookout, Weirs Cove Track' with no description; a minor lookout on the Cape du Couedic strip, no distinct draw named.

name: Bunker Hill Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage itself says it is 'not a significant lookout of any kind'; roadside pull-out.

name: Rocky River Visitor Centre / Flinders Chase Visitor Centre
reason: A visitor centre with a cafe and ticket desk, not an attraction; the park page names it only as where to buy tickets.

name: Koala Walk (Flinders Chase)
reason: Only Wikivoyage names it ('Try your luck'); koalas were removed from Flinders Chase after 2007, so no reliable draw; short roadside walk.

name: Platypus Walk (Rocky River)
reason: For: Wikivoyage names a platypus viewing walk of about an hour from the Flinders Chase visitor centre, a real wildlife activity. Against: single counted source, success depends on dawn/dusk luck, and it lies within Flinders Chase.

name: West Bay
reason: Tourism board singles out West Bay as the island's westernmost inlet at the Rocky River mouth, with sea views and wildlife; a bay a guide names.

name: Hanson Bay
reason: Two counted sources: board says watch the Southern Ocean roll in and beach-walk the dunes to three beaches. (Candidate coordinates are a NZ Hanson Bay: wrong, resolve afresh.)

name: Southern Ocean Lodge
reason: Luxury accommodation, a business not a visitable attraction.

name: Ravine des Casoars
reason: Wilderness protection area beside Cape Borda that the board names for exploring the Valley of the Cassowaries (hiking trail).

name: Cliff Top Hike (Cape Borda)
reason: Short trail from Cape Borda Lightstation per the park page; part of the Cape Borda Lighthouse spot, not a distinct draw.

name: Kelly Hill Conservation Park
reason: Duplicate of Kelly Hill Caves (the Wikivoyage entry for the caves is the attraction in the park).

name: Seal Bay Aquatic Reserve
reason: Duplicate of Seal Bay; marine reserve offshore, no separate visit. No counted source.

name: Southern Kangaroo Island Marine Park
reason: Offshore marine park with a one-line Wikivoyage entry; nothing a visitor can go to as a place (sea lions are seen at Seal Bay).

name: Little Sahara Adventure Centre
reason: Operator (sandboard hire); the place is Little Sahara dunes, listed separately.

name: Kangaroo Island Outdoor Action
reason: Operator (quad bikes, board hire), not a place.

name: Vivonne Bay Conservation Park
reason: No counted source found for the park itself; the draw is Vivonne Bay beach and Harriet River, listed separately (duplicate of Vivonne Bay).

name: Harriet River
reason: Board names the calm river near Vivonne Bay for swimming and kayaking with koala and echidna spotting; distinct from the beach.

name: D'Estrees Bay
reason: Two counted sources: surf and fishing beaches with south coast scenery, a favourite of surfers.

name: D'Estrees Bay Self-guided Drive
reason: A drive route within D'Estrees Bay, part of that spot rather than a place.

name: Cape Gantheaume Conservation Park
reason: Parks SA and the board name the park (wilderness area, walking trails, D'Estrees Bay southern section, Murray Lagoon). Kept as a park with named walks.

name: Murray Lagoon
reason: Wikivoyage and the board name it: wetland with Bald Hill and Timber Creek half-hour to hour walks for birdwatching.

name: Pennington Bay
reason: Wikivoyage says 'don't miss Pennington Bay' and the board features the view; a surf beach on the south coast.

name: Prospect Hill
reason: Both sources: 500-step climb to a 360-degree view, Flinders ascended it in 1802.

name: Pelican Lagoon Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage lists a roadside lookout with no description; minor pull-out on Hog Bay Rd.

name: Pelican Lagoon
reason: For: board names the marine sanctuary for non-motorised paddling and sunrise/sunset. Against: single counted source, essentially the backdrop of American River town, which is a separate candidate.

name: Pelican Lagoon Conservation Park
reason: No counted source found; duplicate of Pelican Lagoon.

name: American River
reason: Both sources give the fishing village its own section: wharf, Independence replica and rebuild shed, walks, wildlife, oysters.

name: American River Oyster Farm Shop
reason: A producer's farm-gate shop; a business, not a place to see.

name: American River Gallery and Arts Centre
reason: Only one board line ('newly opened'); a small gallery, no second source, mere shop-like venue.

name: Independence Trail (American River)
reason: Short in-town trail named in one board paragraph; part of American River, not a distinct draw.

name: Cannery Trail (American River)
reason: Short coastal walk named in one paragraph; part of American River.

name: Glossy black-cockatoo viewing (American River)
reason: Wildlife viewing around town streets and a bird hide, not a discrete place; part of American River.

name: Reeves Point
reason: Both sources: site of South Australia's first settlement, lookout, famous Mulberry Tree, interpretive signs.

name: Flagstaff Hill (Kingscote)
reason: A memorial lookout beside Reeves Point; minor memorial, near-duplicate of Reeves Point.

name: Hope Cottage National Trust Museum
reason: Board names the museum's 'outstanding collection' of island heritage in an 1856 cottage; small museum visitors can enter.

name: Kingscote Silo Art
reason: Board features the 25 m kangaroo and glossy black cockatoo silo mural ('you can't miss'); a roadside icon.

name: Kingscote Art Trail
reason: Diffuse street art across town with no single place; the silo mural is listed separately.

name: Kingscote Jetty
reason: Board names the jetty for fishing, sunset and snorkelling for leafy sea dragons around the pylons; a jetty a guide names.

name: Kingscote Tidal Pool
reason: One passing line among kid-friendly beaches and playgrounds; an ordinary local amenity.
